item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"B is materially closer to the frozen contract because FilesService.Upload delegates to the existing Add method. A reimplements Add’s option handling, request execution, response decoding, and error semantics, directly violating the required reuse path.","reasons":["B’s Upload has the exact requested signature, validates inputs, uses multipartbody.NewFile(\"file\", fileName, content), propagates helper errors, and calls s.Add(ctx, body, contentType, opts...).","Delegating to Add preserves FilesOption behavior and centralizes request and response semantics as explicitly required.","B’s retry test enables RetryAllMethods and supplies a non-seekable reader, matching the reported POST-upload scenario more closely than A’s test.","A duplicates Add internals, including option expansion, headers, Raw.Do, payload decoding, and missing-data handling; this creates maintenance drift despite currently similar behavior."],"risks_a":["Explicitly violates the contract to route Upload through FilesService.Add.","The retry test omits RetryAllMethods: true and does not use a non-seekable source reader.","No tests cover empty filename, nil content, or source-reader failures."],"risks_b":["Adds an unrelated public PersonsService.UploadPicture API and tests, violating scope discipline and the instruction to add exactly the specified convenience API.","The Upload multipart test checks field and filename but never verifies uploaded content.","The retry handler does not inspect the body on both attempts, so the test does not directly prove streamed content was replayed intact after 429 retries; validation and source-reader error tests are also missing."]}
